title: Biology: evolution, diversity, and the environment
author: Sylvia S. Mader

title: Electronics and Communication Engineering Handbook: For ECE Competitive Examinations
author: Susurla V. S. Suresh

title: Indian economic thought: nineteenth century perspectives
author: Birendranath Ganguli

title: Thinner
author: Stephen King
firstSentence: "Thinner," the old Gypsy man with the rotting nose whispers to William Halleck as Halleck and his wife, Heidi, come out of the courthouse.
description: After an overweight lawyer kills an old woman in a hit-and-run and walks free, her father whispers a single word to him — and he begins to lose weight, and keeps losing.

title: Optimizing Exercise and Physical Activity in Older People
author: Adrian Schoo, Meg E. Morris

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
firstSentence: First the colours. Then the humans. That's usually how I see things. Or at least, how I try.
description: Narrated by Death, the story of Liesel Meminger, a foster girl in Nazi Germany who steals books and shares them with the Jewish man hidden in her basement.

title: The real truth about aging: a survival guide for older adults and caregivers
author: Neil Shulman

title: It
author: Stephen King
firstSentence: The terror, which would not end for another twenty-eight years — if it ever did end — began, so far as I know or can tell, with a boat made from a sheet of newspaper floating down a gutter swollen with rain.
description: Seven children in Derry, Maine, confront a shape-shifting evil that hides in the sewers — and, twenty-seven years later, must return as adults to finish it.

title: Atomic Habits: The life-changing million copy bestseller
author: James Clear

title: The office of assertion: an art of rhetoric for the academic essay
author: Scott F. Crider

title: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes
author: Suzanne Collins
firstSentence: Coriolanus released the fistful of cabbage into the pot of boiling water and swore that one day it would never pass his lips again.
description: It is the morning of the reaping that will kick off the tenth annual Hunger Games. Eighteen-year-old Coriolanus Snow is preparing for his one shot at glory as a mentor — assigned the girl tribute from lowly District 12.

title: Sunrise on the Reaping
author: Suzanne Collins
firstSentence: Happy birthday to me.
description: The morning of the reaping for the 50th Hunger Games — the Second Quarter Quell — dawns in District 12, and Haymitch Abernathy is trying not to think about the day ahead.

title: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
firstSentence: When I wake up, the other side of the bed is cold.
description: In the ruins of a place once known as North America lies the nation of Panem, a shining Capitol surrounded by twelve outlying districts. Each year the Capitol forces each district to send one boy and one girl to fight to the death on live television. Sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen volunteers in her sister's place.

title: Catching Fire
author: Suzanne Collins
firstSentence: I clasp the flask between my hands even though the warmth from the tea has long since leached into the frozen air.
description: Katniss Everdeen has won the Hunger Games and returned home to District 12 — but the Capitol is angry, rumours of rebellion are spreading, and the 75th Games bring a twist no victor saw coming.

title: Mockingjay
author: Suzanne Collins
firstSentence: I stare down at my shoes, watching as a fine layer of ash settles on the worn leather.
description: District 12 is gone. Katniss is in District 13, and the rebellion wants her to be the Mockingjay — the symbol of a revolution she never chose to lead.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
firstSentence: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.
description: Elizabeth Bennet, second of five sisters in a family of modest means, meets the proud and wealthy Mr. Darcy — and misjudges him as thoroughly as he misjudges her.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
firstSentence: There was no possibility of taking a walk that day.
description: Orphaned and unloved, Jane Eyre grows up to become a governess at Thornfield Hall, where she falls in love with the brooding Mr. Rochester — who is hiding a terrible secret.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
firstSentence: 1801. — I have just returned from a visit to my landlord — the solitary neighbour that I shall be troubled with.
description: On the wild Yorkshire moors, the foundling Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw form a bond that outlasts marriage, death and a generation of revenge.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
firstSentence: My father's family name being Pirrip, and my Christian name Philip, my infant tongue could make of both names nothing longer or more explicit than Pip.
description: Pip, an orphan raised by his sister in the Kent marshes, is lifted into gentility by an anonymous benefactor — and slowly learns what his great expectations have cost.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
firstSentence: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
description: Against the backdrop of the French Revolution, Charles Darnay and Sydney Carton — two men who look alike and love the same woman — are drawn toward the guillotine.

title: Oliver Twist
author: Charles Dickens
firstSentence: Among other public buildings in a certain town, which for many reasons it will be prudent to refrain from mentioning, there is one anciently common to most towns, great or small: to wit, a workhouse.
description: Born in a workhouse and sold into apprenticeship, Oliver Twist escapes to London and falls in with a gang of child pickpockets run by the Artful Dodger and Fagin.

title: Moby Dick
author: Herman Melville
firstSentence: Call me Ishmael.
description: Ishmael signs aboard the Pequod, a whaling ship commanded by Captain Ahab, who is consumed by his hunt for the white whale that took his leg.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
firstSentence: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I've been turning over in my mind ever since.
description: Nick Carraway rents a cottage on Long Island next to the mansion of Jay Gatsby, a mysterious millionaire who throws lavish parties in the hope that Daisy Buchanan will one day walk in.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
firstSentence: When he was nearly thirteen, my brother Jem got his arm badly broken at the elbow.
description: Scout Finch grows up in Depression-era Alabama while her father, Atticus, defends a Black man falsely accused of assaulting a white woman.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J. D. Salinger
firstSentence: If you really want to hear about it, the first thing you'll probably want to know is where I was born, and what my lousy childhood was like.
description: Expelled from prep school, sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield spends three days wandering New York City, railing against phoniness and mourning a loss he can't name.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
firstSentence: "Christmas won't be Christmas without any presents," grumbled Jo, lying on the rug.
description: Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy March grow from girlhood to womanhood in Civil War-era New England, guided by their mother while their father is away at war.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
firstSentence: You will rejoice to hear that no disaster has accompanied the commencement of an enterprise which you have regarded with such evil forebodings.
description: Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist, creates a sapient creature in an unorthodox experiment — and is destroyed by what he brings to life.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
firstSentence: 3 May. Bistritz.—Left Munich at 8:35 P.M., on 1st May, arriving at Vienna early next morning.
description: Jonathan Harker travels to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy a house in England, and unwittingly helps a vampire loose upon London.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
firstSentence: The studio was filled with the rich odour of roses, and when the light summer wind stirred amidst the trees of the garden, there came through the open door the heavy scent of the lilac.
description: Dorian Gray wishes his portrait would age instead of him. It does — and every sin he commits is recorded on the canvas while his face stays young.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
firstSentence: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do.
description: Alice follows a white rabbit down a hole into a world of talking animals, mad tea parties, and a queen who wants everyone's head.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
firstSentence: Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
description: Anna Karenina, married to a senior official, falls in love with the dashing Count Vronsky and defies Russian society to be with him.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
firstSentence: Many years later, as he faced the firing squad, Colonel Aureliano Buendía was to remember that distant afternoon when his father took him to discover ice.
description: Seven generations of the Buendía family in the town of Macondo, from its founding to its end.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
firstSentence: 124 was spiteful. Full of a baby's venom.
description: Sethe, an escaped slave living in post-Civil-War Ohio, is haunted by the ghost of the daughter she killed rather than see returned to slavery — until a young woman calling herself Beloved arrives at her door.

title: Slaughterhouse-Five
author: Kurt Vonnegut
firstSentence: All this happened, more or less.
description: Billy Pilgrim has come unstuck in time. He survives the firebombing of Dresden, is abducted by aliens, and lives his life out of order.

title: Catch-22
author: Joseph Heller
firstSentence: It was love at first sight.
description: Captain Yossarian wants out of the war. But anyone who wants out must be sane, and anyone sane must fly — that's the catch.

title: Of Mice and Men
author: John Steinbeck
firstSentence: A few miles south of Soledad, the Salinas River drops in close to the hillside bank and runs deep and green.
description: George and Lennie, two migrant workers, dream of owning a piece of land. Then they take a job on a ranch near Soledad.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
author: John Steinbeck
firstSentence: To the red country and part of the gray country of Oklahoma, the last rains came gently, and they did not cut the scarred earth.
description: Driven from their Oklahoma farm by drought and debt, the Joad family joins the migration west to California.

title: The Bell Jar
author: Sylvia Plath
firstSentence: It was a queer, sultry summer, the summer they electrocuted the Rosenbergs, and I didn't know what I was doing in New York.
description: Esther Greenwood, a talented young woman on a magazine internship in New York, feels herself sliding under a bell jar.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
firstSentence: It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen.
description: Winston Smith works at the Ministry of Truth rewriting history for the Party. Then he falls in love, and starts to think for himself.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
firstSentence: Mr. Jones, of the Manor Farm, had locked the hen-houses for the night, but was too drunk to remember to shut the pop-holes.
description: The animals of Manor Farm overthrow their farmer and set up a society of equals — until the pigs start walking on two legs.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
firstSentence: A squat grey building of only thirty-four stories.
description: In a World State where citizens are grown in bottles and kept happy with soma, Bernard Marx begins to feel that something is missing.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
firstSentence: It was a pleasure to burn.
description: Guy Montag is a fireman whose job is to burn books. Then he meets a girl who asks him whether he is happy.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
firstSentence: We slept in what had once been the gymnasium.
description: In the Republic of Gilead, Offred is a Handmaid — valued only for her ovaries — who remembers a time when she had a name, a job and a daughter.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
firstSentence: In the week before their departure to Arrakis, when all the final scurrying about had reached a nearly unbearable frenzy, an old crone came to visit the mother of the boy, Paul.
description: Paul Atreides, heir to a noble house, moves with his family to the desert planet Arrakis — the only source of the spice melange — and into a trap set by their enemies.

title: The Lord of the Rings
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
firstSentence: When Mr. Bilbo Baggins of Bag End announced that he would shortly be celebrating his eleventy-first birthday with a party of special magnificence, there was much talk and excitement in Hobbiton.
description: Frodo Baggins inherits a ring of terrible power and sets out with eight companions to destroy it in the fires of Mount Doom.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
firstSentence: In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit.
description: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit, is talked by the wizard Gandalf into joining thirteen dwarves on a quest to reclaim their treasure from the dragon Smaug.

title: Ender's Game
author: Orson Scott Card
firstSentence: "I've watched through his eyes, I've listened through his ears, and I tell you he's the one."
description: Six-year-old Ender Wiggin is taken to Battle School to be trained as a commander in humanity's war against an alien species.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
firstSentence: The sky above the port was the color of television, tuned to a dead channel.
description: Case, a washed-up hacker, is hired for one last job by a mysterious employer — and finds himself working for an artificial intelligence with plans of its own.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams
firstSentence: Far out in the uncharted backwaters of the unfashionable end of the western spiral arm of the Galaxy lies a small unregarded yellow sun.
description: Seconds before Earth is demolished to make way for a hyperspace bypass, Arthur Dent is rescued by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher for the Guide.

title: Good Omens
author: Neil Gaiman
firstSentence: It was a nice day.
description: An angel and a demon who have grown rather fond of Earth team up to prevent the Apocalypse — if only they could find the Antichrist.

title: American Gods
author: Neil Gaiman
firstSentence: Shadow had done three years in prison.
description: Fresh out of prison, Shadow takes a job as bodyguard to the mysterious Mr. Wednesday and is drawn into a war between the old gods and the new.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
firstSentence: "What's two plus two?"
description: Ryland Grace wakes up alone on a spaceship with no memory of who he is or why he's there. He has to remember, because the fate of the Earth depends on it.

title: The Shining
author: Stephen King
firstSentence: Jack Torrance thought: Officious little prick.
description: Jack Torrance takes a job as winter caretaker of the Overlook Hotel, bringing his wife and his psychically gifted son — and the hotel begins to work on him.

title: The Stand
author: Stephen King
firstSentence: Sally.
description: A weaponised flu escapes a lab and kills almost everyone. The survivors dream of two figures — an old woman in Nebraska and a dark man in Las Vegas — and choose sides.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
firstSentence: When I think of my wife, I always think of her head.
description: On their fifth wedding anniversary, Amy Dunne disappears. Her husband Nick becomes the prime suspect — and the story is told by both of them.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
firstSentence: In the corner of a first-class smoking carriage, Mr. Justice Wargrave, lately retired from the bench, puffed at a cigar and ran an interested eye through the political news in the Times.
description: Ten strangers are lured to an island off the Devon coast, and one by one they die, according to the words of a nursery rhyme.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
firstSentence: Mr. Sherlock Holmes, who was usually very late in the mornings, save upon those not infrequent occasions when he was up all night, was seated at the breakfast table.
description: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson investigate the death of Sir Charles Baskerville, and the legend of a spectral hound that haunts his family.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
firstSentence: It was five o'clock on a winter's morning in Syria.
description: A snowdrift stops the Orient Express, and in the morning a passenger is found stabbed to death. Hercule Poirot is on board.

title: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
author: John le Carré

title: Where the Crawdads Sing
author: Delia Owens
firstSentence: Marsh is not swamp.
description: Kya Clark, abandoned as a child, raises herself in the marshes of North Carolina — and years later is accused of murdering a young man from town.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
firstSentence: When I was born, the name for what I was did not exist.
description: Circe, daughter of the sun god Helios, is banished to a deserted island where she hones her witchcraft and crosses paths with Odysseus.

title: The Song of Achilles
author: Madeline Miller
firstSentence: My father was a king and the son of kings.
description: Patroclus, an awkward young prince exiled to Phthia, befriends the golden Achilles — and follows him to Troy.

title: Pachinko
author: Min Jin Lee
firstSentence: History has failed us, but no matter.
description: Four generations of a Korean family in Japan, from a boarding house in Busan to the pachinko parlours of Osaka, bound by love, sacrifice and the long shadow of exile.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
firstSentence: When he woke in the woods in the dark and the cold of the night he'd reach out to touch the child sleeping beside him.
description: A father and his young son walk south through a burned America, carrying a pistol and pushing a shopping cart with everything they own.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
firstSentence: The boy's name was Santiago.
description: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd, dreams of treasure at the Egyptian pyramids and sets out to find it.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
firstSentence: About 13.5 billion years ago, matter, energy, time and space came into being in what is known as the Big Bang.
description: How Homo sapiens came to dominate the planet — through the cognitive, agricultural and scientific revolutions.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
firstSentence: My strongest memory is not a memory.
description: Born to survivalists in the mountains of Idaho, Tara Westover never set foot in a classroom until she taught herself enough to get into university.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
firstSentence: On an exceptionally hot evening early in July a young man came out of the garret in which he lodged in S. Place and walked slowly, as though in hesitation, towards K. bridge.
description: Raskolnikov, a destitute former student, murders a pawnbroker to prove a theory — and is undone by his conscience.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
firstSentence: Once when I was six years old I saw a magnificent picture in a book, called True Stories from Nature, about the primeval forest.
description: A pilot stranded in the Sahara meets a small boy from a tiny asteroid, who tells him about the planets he has visited and the rose he left behind.

title: The Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
firstSentence: As Gregor Samsa awoke one morning from uneasy dreams he found himself transformed in his bed into a gigantic insect.
description: Gregor Samsa, a travelling salesman, wakes up as an insect. His family adjusts.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
firstSentence: Marley was dead: to begin with.
description: Ebenezer Scrooge, a miser who despises Christmas, is visited by the ghost of his partner and three spirits who show him his past, present and the future that awaits him.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
firstSentence: The family of Dashwood had long been settled in Sussex.
description: When Mr. Dashwood dies, his wife and three daughters are left with almost nothing. Elinor's sense and Marianne's sensibility are tested by two very different suitors.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
firstSentence: Emma Woodhouse, handsome, clever, and rich, with a comfortable home and happy disposition, seemed to unite some of the best blessings of existence.
description: Emma Woodhouse, convinced of her talent for matchmaking, meddles in the romantic lives of everyone around her — with consequences she never sees coming.

title: Death on the Nile
author: Agatha Christie
firstSentence: Linnet Ridgeway!
description: On a cruise up the Nile, a wealthy heiress is shot dead in her cabin. Hercule Poirot, on holiday, must find the killer before the boat docks.

title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson

title: The Goldfinch
author: Donna Tartt
firstSentence: While I was still in Amsterdam, I dreamed about my mother for the first time in years.
description: Theo Decker, thirteen, survives an explosion at the Met that kills his mother, and walks out with a small Dutch painting that will shape the rest of his life.
